title: Stop Sending Me Your Errors
excerpt: On the tragic misuse of the multipart/alternative MIME type in present-day email traffic.
content_html:
My desktop email client of choice can render both text/plain and text/html emails. I happen to prefer text/plain versions. And you're right, I should get with the times. But when you misuse multipart/alternative to send me an error, you're not helping me or anyone else for that matter. In fact, you're doing the exact opposite.

The ancient scrolls document multipart/alternative as a way to present the same information in multiple interchangeable forms. Most commonly, this is used to send the HTML version of an email alongside its plain text counterpart.

In other words, multipart/alternative is NOT FOR SENDING ME YOUR DAMNED ERRORS. If my email client cannot handle your email, it's the client's job to report such errors.

This morning, I received an email with the body:

Plain text version not available

After switching to the HTML version, I was not greeted with a rendered equivalent of:

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
    <head>
        <title>...</title>
    </head>
    <body>
        <p>Plain text version not available</p>
    </body>
</html>

Instead, I was greeted with actual email content. I would have been surprised if this weren't so common.

Let's consider the scenarios where a user would be presented with the text/plain version:

  1. Scenario: They're using an ancient pre-MIME email client because they are a time traveller from the '80s.

    Result: They see some gibberish, followed by "Plain text version not available", followed by HTML-looking gibberish. If they don't already know what's happening, then this message isn't going to help them fix anything. That's assuming they even spot it among the gibberish.

  2. Scenario: They're using a MIME-capable email client which can't handle text/html.

    Result: They see this "error", and since their client understands MIME, it infers that this "error" is supposedly interchangeable with the bit it can't understand and presents it. Maybe the client offers a way to grab the HTML, or maybe not. The user might not even understand that the situation is recoverable.

    If there were no text/plain part, their client would probably do no worse than your "error" message, and might even offer an actual recovery path instead. And if it did do worse, you should again ask yourself whether your message would actually help them.

  3. Scenario: They're using a MIME-capable email client which can handle both text/html and text/plain, but they configured it to prefer text/plain.

    Result: Very similar to scenario 2, except they would have immediately gotten the intended experience if you had simply not added an error as a text/plain part.

    Now they must rely on their understanding of the situation and knowledge of their email client to find the option to switch to the format they explicitly configured it not to prefer. You just made their life more difficult.

If your email system cannot generate a useful text/plain version of the email, then it doesn't help anyone to tell them that. If scenario 1 sounded desirable to you1, you could instead use HTML comments to give the victims of your HTML email more or less an equivalently confusing experience, without ignoring the RFC or pissing off random internet nobodies.

"But," I hear you cry, "I put the text/plain version first and the text/html version last. Just like the scrolls said I should do to indicate my preferred representation."

That's cool. I get that you prefer HTML, but I prefer plain text. When multipart/alternative is used correctly, the plain text part can be much cleaner than anything I can render from the HTML part. If I didn't register my preference for text/plain with my email client, I would face the mirror image of scenario 3.

Thankfully, there's an easy solution to all of this: just stop sending text/plain alternatives that are not, in fact, alternatives. Not only will it make all 10 of us happy, but it can also help avoid getting your email marked as spam.

It doesn't even stop at errors. Here are some more (verbatim, aside from bits in [square brackets]) examples of real text/plain parts of multipart/alternative emails I've received recently:

This email contains html content. Please configure your email client for html or visit <site.website>[sic] for latest show times.

text/html

Use
it before it’s gone
[50 blank lines]
[... a bit more content ...] [... random CSS stylesheet oneliner ...]
[100 more blank lines]
[... et cetera ...]

[title]
Hi Tom /,
Thanks for your order!
[date]
Your receipt is attached to this email.
If you do not want to receive receipts by email, you can <a style="text-decoration:none;" href="https://[domain]/optOut/receiptOptOut?businessId=[id]&emailAddress=[my-email]&token=[token]">unsubscribe<a/>.

Footnotes

  1. I very much doubt that anyone who would be confused by this situation is using an email client without MIME support, or even without text/html support in 2026.↩

content_html_zh:
我选择的桌面电子邮件客户端可以呈现文本/纯文本和文本/html 电子邮件。 我碰巧更喜欢文本/纯文本版本。 你是对的，我应该与时俱进。 但是，当您滥用 multipart/alternative 向我发送错误时，您并没有在这方面帮助我或其他任何人。 事实上，你所做的恰恰相反。

古代卷轴记录了多部分/替代，作为以多种可互换形式呈现相同信息的方式。 最常见的是，这用于发送电子邮件的 HTML 版本及其纯文本副本。

换句话说，multipart/alternative 不是为了向我发送你该死的错误。 如果我的电子邮件客户端无法处理您的电子邮件，则客户端有责任报告此类错误。

今天早上，我收到一封包含正文的电子邮件：

纯文本版本不可用

切换到 HTML 版本后，我没有看到类似的渲染结果：

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
    <head>
        <title>...</title>
    </head>
    <body>
        <p>Plain text version not available</p>
    </body>
</html>

相反，我收到的是实际的电子邮件内容。 如果这种情况不是很常见，我会感到惊讶。

让我们考虑向用户呈现文本/纯文本版本的场景：

  1. 场景：他们正在使用古老的 MIME 之前的电子邮件客户端，因为他们是 80 年代的时间旅行者。 结果：他们看到一些乱码，然后是“纯文本版本不可用”，然后是看起来 HTML 的乱码。 如果他们还不知道发生了什么，那么此消息不会帮助他们解决任何问题。 假设他们甚至在乱码中发现了它。
  2. 场景：他们使用的是支持 MIME 的电子邮件客户端，但无法处理文本/html。 结果：他们看到这个“错误”，并且由于他们的客户端理解 MIME，因此它推断这个“错误”可以与它无法理解的位互换并呈现它。 也许客户端提供了一种获取 HTML 的方法，也可能不提供。 用户甚至可能不知道这种情况是可以恢复的。 如果没有文本/纯文本部分，他们的客户端可能不会比您的“错误”消息更糟糕，甚至可能提供实际的恢复路径。 如果情况确实更糟，你应该再次问问自己，你的信息是否真的能帮助他们。
  3. 场景：他们使用支持 MIME 的电子邮件客户端，该客户端可以处理 text/html 和 text/plain，但他们将其配置为更喜欢 text/plain。 结果：与场景 2 非常相似，但如果您没有将错误添加为文本/纯文本部分，他们会立即获得预期的体验。 现在，他们必须依靠对情况的理解和电子邮件客户端的知识来找到切换到他们明确配置为不喜欢的格式的选项。 你只是让他们的生活变得更加困难。

如果您的电子邮件系统无法生成有用的文本/纯文本版本的电子邮件，那么告诉任何人这一点都没有帮助。 如果场景 1 听起来适合您1，您可以使用 HTML 注释来为您的 HTML 电子邮件的受害者提供或多或少同样令人困惑的体验，而无需忽略 RFC 或激怒随机的互联网小人物。

“但是，”我听到你哭了，“我把文本/纯文本版本放在第一位，文本/html 版本放在最后。 就像卷轴所说的那样，我应该表明我喜欢的代表方式。”

这很酷。 我知道您更喜欢 HTML，但我更喜欢纯文本。 当正确使用 multipart/alternative 时，纯文本部分可能比我从 HTML 部分渲染的任何内容都要干净得多。 如果我没有在电子邮件客户端中注册我对文本/纯文本的偏好，我将面临场景 3 的镜像。

值得庆幸的是，有一个简单的解决方案可以解决所有这些问题：只需停止发送实际上不是替代方案的文本/普通替代方案即可。 它不仅会让我们 10 个人都高兴，而且还可以帮助避免您的电子邮件被标记为垃圾邮件。

它甚至不会因错误而停止。 以下是我最近收到的多部分/替代电子邮件的真实文本/纯文本部分的更多示例（逐字记录，除了[方括号]中的位）：
